chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abu al-Husayn al-Nakha'i, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The cow and the camel are sufficient for seven [people] in the cities, but in Mina they are sufficient for only one [person].
ai.seo_question: How many people can share one cow or camel for Hajj sacrifice in Mina versus other cities?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the geographical distinction in Hajj sacrificial rules, noting that while a single cow or camel can suffice for seven people in major cities (al-amsar), the stricter standard applies in Mina where one animal is required per person. This ruling reflects the scholarly consensus on the specific location of the sacrifice during the Hajj rituals, emphasizing the sanctity of Mina as the primary site for the Udhiyah. The distinction highlights the practical application of fiqh principles regarding the validity of shared sacrifices based on location.
